source.title: Two Refusals or One? Disentangling Safety and Epistemic Abstention Directions in Language Model Activations

record.tranche_reason: Extracts a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction and intervenes on it in activation space, measuring refusal on another model and prompt setting. The intervention is restricted to selected layers rather than the original all-layer, all-position removal.
record.gate_note: The study reports cross-ablation outcomes for safety refusal and epistemic abstention, plus geometry comparing those two directions. It does not test adding a direction, weight edits, jailbreak mechanisms, or general capabilities. The quantization results concern direction drift, not a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: Extracts a harmful-minus-benign (AdvBench vs Alpaca) difference-in-means direction following Arditi et al. and projects it out of residual-stream activations in NF4 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It measures keyword-detected refusal and an off-target behaviour (epistemic abstention). This is the original's removal test. Differences: removal is at selected layers only, with strength swept (α up to 2.0, i.e. beyond pure projection), and there is no addition test or general-capability evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that safety refusal and epistemic abstention are not mediated by the same dominant direction. Safety ablation (best at k=1, α=1.5) strongly removes refusal while abstention is preserved. They frame the result as evidence against a shared direction, not proof of independent circuitry, and note the epistemic handle is weak.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-versus-benign difference-in-means extraction and directional projection, but performs activation-space cross-ablation only at selected residual blocks and sweeps strength rather than removing the direction at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies with ablation strength and number of targeted layers: single-layer, unit-strength safety ablation has a small effect, while the reported single-layer α=1.5 setting produces a large reduction.

fits_no_version.finding: The safety and epistemic-abstention difference-in-means directions are near-orthogonal. Llama mean cosine is 0.049 and max 0.183; peak layers are 22 vs 9. Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2-9B have cosines of −0.039 and 0.123 at their top safety layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The safety refusal direction is geometrically distinct from an epistemic-abstention direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the epistemic direction changes abstention by at most 0.02. A held-out linear probe nonetheless reaches 1.00 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epistemic abstention is linearly decodable but not mediated by a single removable difference-in-means direction.

fits_no_version.finding: The safety direction re-extracted under NF4 and INT8 keeps cosine 0.994 and 0.962 to the FP16 direction. The epistemic direction keeps 0.978 and 0.935.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is stable under weight quantization.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
record.problems: Refusal and abstention are detected by keyword matching, so paraphrases may be missed. The study uses a small replication set; epistemic prompts may confound knowledge limits with reading-comprehension difficulty. Cross-ablation is asymmetric, and the strongest result is an activation-space intervention on n=50 prompts per group. General capabilities are not evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: The full per-layer geometry table (Appendix B, Table 1) is not itemized layer by layer; aggregate mean, extrema, and peak-layer results are retained in r20–r22. Quantization-drift measurements are omitted because they do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Removal at all layers and positions. Weight-level ablation. General capability or benchmark retention. Models other than Llama-3.1-8B for causal tests (Qwen and Gemma are geometry only).
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No jailbreak mechanism test or adversarial training.
No test of whether safety refusal itself is multi-directional.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No transfer of a direction across languages, models, or base/instruct. Quantized variants are re-extracted and compared by cosine, not transferred.

missing.what: E→S cross-contamination: effect of epistemic-direction ablation on safety refusal (0.00–0.06; headline CI [−0.06, 0.06]). Not version-relevant, but part of the grid.
Quantization drift of the safety direction: NF4 cosine 0.994, INT8 0.962 to FP16; separability 0.760 and 0.781. Omitted by the reader; possibly relevant to direction stability across model variants.
Qualitative evidence that the ablated model switches to procedural compliance on harmful prompts. This addresses the concern that the keyword detector misses refusals.

record.verdict_notes: All causal rows come from a single NF4-loaded Llama-3.1-8B, with n=50 per group and keyword detection. α>1 overshoots pure projection, so the best setting is not the original's orthogonal ablation. The finding that targeting more layers (k=2,4) weakens removal is unexplained and suggests fragility. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests activation-space removal of the safety difference-in-means direction, but not addition, ablation at every layer and position, or broad general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration.
No test of jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
The study compares a safety direction with an epistemic-abstention direction; it does not test whether safety refusal itself is affine, conic, or supported by multiple directions.
No measure of harmfulness judgment separate from refusal.
Additional model families are probed separately; the study does not transfer one extracted direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (NF4), single top-separability layer 22, α=1.5 or 2.0
relationships.reason: Removing the direction cuts refusal 0.98→0.16 (r1) and drop 0.80 (r4). Epistemic abstention is kept (0.82→0.88, CI spans zero) in r2, r12 and r11, with a somewhat larger shift at α=2.0 (r13).
relationships.display_finding: Removal reduced refusal from 0.98 to 0.16, with another setting yielding a 0.80 decrease; epistemic abstention changed from 0.82 to 0.88 with a confidence interval spanning zero, though α=2.0 produced a somewhat larger shift.

source_check.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (NF4), single top-separability layer 22, α=1.5 or 2.0
source_check.reason: At k=1, α=1.5 refusal falls 0.98->0.16; at α=2.0 the drop is 0.80. Abstention goes 0.82->0.88, with the cross-contamination CI spanning zero. The reason wrongly cites r11, which is α=1.0 and outside this group. Removal needs α>1 and stays incomplete.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, α=1.0 at one layer, or k=2/4 targeted layers at any α
relationships.reason: Refusal barely moves (drops 0.02–0.12): r3, r5–r7 negligible, r8–r10 small. Removal depends strongly on layer count and strength, and more layers gave weaker effects. Even the best setting leaves 0.16 refusal (r1).
relationships.display_finding: The tested settings reduced refusal by only 0.02–0.12, with more targeted layers producing weaker effects; even the best setting left 0.16 refusal.

relation.reason: Its own cross-ablation results show how far removing the safety direction lowers refusal, and whether an off-target behaviour (epistemic abstention) is kept.

tranche.reason: Uses the same harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means extraction as Arditi et al. (AdvBench vs Alpaca, last token) and the same kind of keyword refusal measure. The intervention is a close variant: projection removal at 1-4 selected layers with an α sweep.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] verdict ids, so l1 and l2 follow pack order. Single run on NF4 Llama, ablation at 1-4 layers only, keyword detection, n=50. The absent (0.04) vs partial (0.08) cut is the reader's own, not the study's. Safety-direction quantization drift vs FP16 (cos 0.994 for NF4, 0.962 for INT8) may bear on V6 (model variants).

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (NF4), keyword refusal detection, n=50. Ablation applied only at the top safety layer (layer 22, k=1). α=1.0: drop 0.02 (0.98->0.96). α=1.5: 0.98->0.16. α=2.0: drop 0.80. At k=2 or 4 layers, drops are 0.04-0.12 at every α. No all-layer ablation was tested.
statements.problem: The Llama numbers are right but the statement leaves out that the ablation was at a single layer (k=1). Readers may take 'exact ablation not enough' to mean the original all-layer ablation, which this study never ran.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, single safety layer at α=1.5
reader_labels.reason: Removing the safety direction substantially lowers refusal while epistemic abstention does not collapse (r1–r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The headline intervention leaves refusal at 0.16, unit-strength removal changes refusal only slightly, and the study does not test all-layer/all-position removal, addition, or general capabilities (r1, r3–r10).
